messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with specific facilities. We need to call the function for each city. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location string and facilities which can be one of "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities field expects a single value? It says type public_library_find_nearby = (_: { location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[], }) => any; So facilities can be either a string among those or an array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe". But the union includes "Cafe"[] as a type. So we can pass either a string or an array of "Cafe". For multiple facilities, maybe we need to call multiple times? The function only accepts one facility at a time. So we need to call it separately for each requirement.

We have three separate requests:

1. New York with Reading Room and Fiction. So we need two calls: one for Reading Room, one for Fiction.

2. Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and Children Section. Two calls.

3. Chicago with Cafe and Reading Room. Two calls.

Thus total six calls.

We should output the function calls sequentially.
